Version Packages
Correctness, performance, API-conformance

perf(algorithms): run hot algorithm loops on a CSR snapshot

Closeness, betweenness, PageRank, HITS, eigenvector, and connected
components now run on a compressed-sparse-row arc snapshot (Int32Array
arcs, integer node positions) instead of Map-based id adjacency.

Measured on 2k nodes / 6k edges: closeness 2575ms -> 73ms, betweenness
4597ms -> 169ms, HITS 202ms -> 4ms, PageRank 26ms -> 2ms; connected
components on 100k nodes: 379ms -> 7ms. Head-to-head on identical
graphs: faster than graphology for betweenness (1.7x), PageRank, and
components (2x).

The snapshot caches per GraphIndex + a new version counter (bumped by
every structural API mutation, including per-edge mode changes), so it
inherits the index staleness contract unchanged. tests/csr.test.ts
pins all eight invalidation paths; a thresholded betweenness test
guards the CSR path in CI.

refactor(core): shared compile-time-guarded entity-config cloning

toNodeConfig/toEdgeConfig in src/config.ts replace three hand-rolled
field enumerations (diff, transforms, MST output). An exhaustiveness
assertion makes adding a field to GraphNode/GraphEdge a compile error
until the clone functions handle it — closing the silent-field-drop
bug class that produced four instances across prior sessions.

Also fixes MST output sharing port objects with the source graph.

feat(algorithms): Louvain, max-flow/min-cut, dominators, transitive reduction

- getLouvainCommunities: deterministic two-phase Louvain modularity
  optimization (undirected semantics, weighted, resolution option)
- getMaxFlow: Edmonds-Karp with min-cut edges; capacities from weight;
  non-directed edges carry capacity both ways (CLRS 26.1 verified)
- getDominatorTree: Cooper-Harvey-Kennedy immediate dominators,
  mode-aware (for statecharts: which states every path from the
  initial state must pass through)
- getTransitiveReduction: minimal equivalent DAG; descriptive errors
  on cycles or non-directed edges; all entity fields preserved

40 known-answer tests with sources stated in comments.

test: differential suite vs graphology + randomized self-properties

158 tests on seeded random graphs: graphology as oracle for connected
components, Dijkstra distances, PageRank, degrees, and betweenness
(each verified on a hand-checked example before the random loop; one
pinned intentional divergence: non-directed self-loop degree). Plus
self-properties: override-equivalence, reverseGraph involution,
diff->patch convergence under random API mutations, hasPath <=>
getShortestPath, prim == kruskal. Zero discrepancies found.

Adds graphology + plugin packages as devDependencies.
docs: session analysis/summary, README algorithms + perf notes, changeset

perf(algorithms): CSR pathfinding + polynomial mixed-graph acyclicity

Dijkstra/BFS shortest paths and A* run on the CSR snapshot (50k nodes /
200k edges: single-target dijkstra 329ms -> 58ms, A* 27ms -> 7ms;
all-targets 514ms -> 342ms, now reconstruction-bound). Differential
Dijkstra oracle re-validates results.

isAcyclic on mixed graphs gains polynomial fast paths (directed-only
cycle, union-find over non-directed edges, SCC singleton check); exact
enumeration only runs inside ambiguous multi-node SCCs. A 2^30-path
acyclic mixed graph that previously hung resolves in milliseconds.

fix: malformed-input hardening + getGraphIssues

- getAncestors/getDescendants/getDepth/getLCA terminate on authored
  parentId cycles (stop at first repeated node, documented)
- new zod-free getGraphIssues(graph) core export: structural invariant
  checks with entity-naming messages and machine-readable codes;
  schemas' validateGraph delegates its invariant portion to it
- mermaid/state: _region_ detection requires the exact structural
  pattern under a parallel parent; user ids containing the substring
  are no longer dropped
docs: getGraphIssues README section, summary addendum, changeset
chore: bump heavy-results-shake to major with migration notes

Merge pull request #22 from statelyai/graph-improvements

Correctness audit fixes, CSR performance core, differential testing, new algorithms

perf(algorithms): CSR bfs/dfs generators + single-target early exit

Harness-driven fixes: bfs full sweep on 100k nodes/300k edges dropped
623ms -> 4.4ms (was the slowest of five libraries, now the fastest);
single-target shortest-path queries early-exit the search once every
node at the target's distance is settled, preserving all equal-cost
tie paths including through zero-weight edges (tested).

feat(bench): cross-library benchmark harness

pnpm bench:compare runs seeded identical graphs (random, scale-free,
grid, layered-DAG x 1k/10k/100k) through @statelyai/graph, graphology,
ngraph, graphlib, and headless cytoscape via each library's idiomatic
public API. Median-of-runs timing, crash/too-slow capture, markdown +
JSON reports in bench/compare/results/. Adds competitor devDeps.

perf(algorithms): bidirectional Dijkstra for single-pair shortest paths

Forward search on traversable arcs, backward on reverse arcs, Pohl
termination (topF + topB >= mu). 50k-node random graph point query:
58ms -> 0.8ms; now 2.2x faster than graphology's bidirectional
implementation in the harness (was 60x slower unidirectional).

Negative weights are now detected up front for sublinear searches
(single-pair, early-exit, A*): O(1) via a CSR-cached flag for default
weights, one O(m) sweep for custom getWeight. Previously a sublinear
search could terminate without scanning a reachable negative edge and
silently return a wrong path (caught by an existing test); now the
throw-on-negative contract holds regardless of search order.

Optimize algorithm hot paths with typed-array CSR kernels (#34)

* Optimize algorithm hot paths with typed-array CSR kernels

Rewrites the algorithm hot paths onto typed-array CSR kernels: iterative
Tarjan SCC, Kahn toposort with cached in-degrees, CSR-direct bipartite
coloring, compact-arc Bellman-Ford (plus a single-pair fast path),
flat-matrix Floyd-Warshall with copy-on-write tie lists, chunked
hand-rolled BFS/DFS/postorder iterators, cached per-arc default weights
for Dijkstra/A*/bidirectional search, a per-version degree map, and
O(length) shortest-path materialization via a shared backtracking buffer.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Ramp traversal chunk sizes so early-exit consumers stay lazy

BFS/DFS batches start at 8 nodes and double up to 1024, so taking the
first few nodes of a huge graph costs a few nodes of traversal (plus the
same O(n) visited/queue allocation the generator implementation paid),
while full traversals keep amortized chunked speed.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01QXF7Ba1P2JvvtCfiYbX9xe

* Fix zero-weight self-loop crash in Floyd-Warshall; drop memo retention

Floyd-Warshall no longer records tying self-loops as predecessors — the
sparse diagonal cell made the old push crash, and recording them would
let tie merging build self-referential lists that hang reconstruction.
Negative self-loops still surface via the negative-cycle check, and
reconstruction now carries the same on-path guard as the Dijkstra-side
enumeration. Adds regression tests for both shapes.

The one-entry index memo now holds WeakRefs, so it never extends the
lifetime of the most recently queried graph.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01QXF7Ba1P2JvvtCfiYbX9xe

* Patch CSR node snapshot when updateNode replaces a node object

updateNode swaps the node object in place (same id/position, arrays
untouched), which no version or staleness check can observe — the CSR's
cached node snapshot kept serving the pre-update object to fresh
traversals. The index now notifies derived caches of node replacement
and the CSR patches the one slot in O(1), so traversals stay both fast
and current. Adds a regression test.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01QXF7Ba1P2JvvtCfiYbX9xe

* Close buffered traversal state on iterator throw()

The BFS/DFS fast serve paths check their cursors before the finished
flag, so an injected throw() left buffered nodes servable. return() and
throw() now share a close() hook that drops buffered output, matching
generator exhaustion semantics. Adds a regression test for both.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01QXF7Ba1P2JvvtCfiYbX9xe

* Exhaust traversal iterators when lazy setup throws

Setup errors (e.g. radius validation) left the iterator half-initialized
with started=true; a second next() on the postorder iterator then hit
undefined internal state instead of returning done. Setup now runs
through a shared ensureStarted() that marks the iterator finished on
failure, matching generator semantics for all three traversals. Adds a
regression test.
